previous_statement: A connected component of a smooth manifold is open, so calU_e is an open smooth submanifold of calU. Because mu and sigma are continuous, mu(calU_e x calU_e) is connected and contains mu(J,J)=J, while sigma(calU_e) is connected and contains sigma(J)=J; hence both images lie in calU_e. Likewise U(1) x calU_e is connected and its image under the smooth scalar action contains J, so that action preserves calU_e. It is free: a unitary U has a right inverse and so U is nonzero, whence cU=U implies c=1. It is proper: for the action graph map (c,U)|->(cU,U), the inverse image of a compact K is a closed subset of the compact set U(1) x pr_2(K). Thus lem-topology-quotient-manifold gives the quotient map p:calU_e->breve-calU as a smooth surjective submersion; its uniqueness identifies this quotient smooth structure with the one used by lem-stage1-quotient-manifold-package. Equivariance gives p(mu(cU,dV))=p(mu(U,V)) and p(sigma(cU))=p(sigma(U)), so the displayed breve-mu and breve-sigma are well-defined. They are smooth: local smooth sections of the submersions p x p and p express them locally as p o mu o (s_1,s_2) and p o sigma o s, and equivariance makes these local expressions agree. Finally (A_5) gives breve-mu(breve-e,[U])=[U]=breve-mu([U],breve-e) and breve-sigma(breve-e)=breve-e.
new_statement: A connected component of a smooth manifold is open, so calU_e is an open smooth submanifold of calU. The smooth scalar action restricts to a smooth, free, proper U(1)-action on calU_e, and lem-topology-quotient-manifold equips the orbit space breve-calU:=calU_e/U(1), with its quotient topology, with the unique smooth structure for which p:calU_e->breve-calU is a smooth surjective submersion. We choose this quotient-theorem smooth structure. The manifold supplied by lem-stage1-quotient-manifold-package has the same underlying orbit space and quotient topology. Its connectedness and compactness therefore persist; its dimension, absence of boundary, and orientability transfer to the chosen structure through the topology-invariant local-homology orientation system. Equivariance then makes breve-mu([U],[V]):=[mu(U,V)] and breve-sigma([U]):=[sigma(U)] well-defined, and local smooth sections of p x p and p make them smooth. Finally breve-mu(breve-e,[U])=[U]=breve-mu([U],breve-e) and breve-sigma(breve-e)=breve-e.
